plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Ribbons of scarlet, canary yellow, blush pink and deep purple stripe the flat Dutch bulb fields. They shimmer like a painted quilt under wide spring skies. Each cup-shaped bloom opens wide in the sun and closes again at dusk.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-May, usually at its best in mid-April
plants.location: Bulb-growing region of the Netherlands, including Keukenhof Gardens near Lisse
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs sparked 'tulip mania' in the Dutch Republic, and single bulbs sold for more than the price of a canal house.

plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: Each spring, whole hillsides and roadsides across Texas turn a rich cobalt blue. Dense spikes of pea-like flowers are tipped with a crisp white cap that fades to wine-red as the bloom ages. A light honey-sweet scent hangs over the meadows.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak from late March to mid-April
plants.location: Central Texas and the Texas Hill Country, USA
plants.funFact: The white tip on each flower turns reddish-purple after pollination. This signals to bees that the flower no longer has nectar to give.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: This vigorous twining vine drapes fences, pergolas and tree limbs in long, fragrant, hanging clusters of violet flowers. The blooms open before the feathery leaves fully unfurl, so the display looks like a lavender waterfall.
plants.location: Gardens and woodland edges of the eastern United States, such as Virginia, and its native China
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine and can grow strong enough to crush wooden structures. Chinese wisteria is also invasive in parts of North America, where it can smother native trees.
